subject: Conditional traffic swap & auto-revert request — MediaWorks migration
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mediaworks.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional traffic swap & auto-revert request — MediaWorks migration

Hi Irene,

Quick context: we plan to move a controlled subset of Live traffic (initially 5–10%) to Redwood next week as part of our model migration. The goal is to validate latency and inference cost in production before a full cutover.

Request: MediaWorks is asking Redwood for an operational agreement that lets us do a conditional traffic swap with an automated revert/pin policy if latency or error rates cross agreed thresholds. Specifically:
- Allow a staged traffic shift (5% -> 10% over 2 hours) with runtime-controlled pinning of the prior stable model if p50 or p95 latency degrades beyond thresholds.
- Support automatic fallback to the previously pinned version (no manual intervention) if the circuit breaker trips.
- Documented SLO carve-out for the canary window and a short exception that keeps our renewal SLA intact if we follow the process.

I've attached our migration plan (mediaworks_migration_plan_v1.pdf). OpsSRE is included here for telemetry/alerting details.

Can Redwood confirm whether we can get a one-off SLA exception for this progressive swap and what telemetry/alerting hooks you need from our side? If possible, outline the fallback/pin behavior you propose so we can sign it off.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
VP, Platform Engineering
MediaWorks

Attachments: mediaworks_migration_plan_v1.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mediaworks.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional traffic swap & auto-revert request — MediaWorks migration

Laura / Marcus — FYI and asking for a quick approval path.

Elena from MediaWorks wants a documented SLA carve-out and an operational agreement that permits an automated revert/pinning flow during a staged traffic shift. Key asks from their side: 5->10% shift over 2 hours, auto-fallback to prior stable model if latency/error thresholds breach, and an exception to the standard SLA during the canary window provided we meet telemetry requirements.

Proposed Redwood guardrails (high level):
- Circuit breaker evaluates a rolling 5-minute window. If p95 latency > 1.8x baseline OR error rate > 0.8% absolute, trigger immediate traffic revert to prior pinned model.
- Revert is automatic at the routing layer; the prior stable model (version pin) must be available in the same region.
- No permanent pin without a documented post-mortem and a sign-off from our SRE/CS teams.
- Require MediaWorks to emit a canary tag and the following traces/metrics to our tracing and alerting endpoints: request_id, model_version, request_duration_ms, token_count.

Can we accept this as an SLA exception for MediaWorks under Deal MW-2026-0943? If so I’ll draft the short form exception and attach our required telemetry checklist for them to sign.

—Irene
Product, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional traffic swap & auto-revert request — MediaWorks migration

Thanks for the write-up, Irene. I like the structure but want to tighten the thresholds and add a short cooling period. My suggestions:

- Thresholds: p95 latency > 1.6x baseline OR sustained p50 > 2x for 3 consecutive 1-minute samples -> mark as degraded. Error rate > 0.5% absolute (not relative) should also be treated as a breaker.
- Cooling: when the breaker triggers and we auto-revert, we gate any re-attempts for at least 30 minutes unless the canary is explicitly re-opened by MediaWorks with a remediation note.
- Pin semantics: auto-revert pins to the last known-good minor version; pin duration limited to 24 hours unless extended by written sign-off from Redwood CS + MediaWorks.
- Observability: require a dedicated canary dashboard (we'll create a per-route dashboard in Console) and an alert to on-call that includes the latest 100 traces and a CSV of recent latency percentiles.

I'll attach the short-form SLA exception template and the telemetry checklist. If Marcus signs off on the routing changes and SRE pieces, I think we can push this through as a single exception under the Sales-approved playbook.

Attaching: signed_sla_exception_form.docx (draft) — attach in final once MediaWorks signs.

—Laura
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional traffic swap & auto-revert request — MediaWorks migration

Elena — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we've agreed to the following operational commitments for the MediaWorks migration:

1) Traffic plan: 5% -> 10% over 2 hours (explicit steps in the attached short form).
2) Breaker criteria: p95 > 1.6x baseline OR sustained p50 > 2x for 3 consecutive 1-minute samples OR error rate > 0.5% absolute -> automatic revert to last-known-good minor version.
3) Cooling: auto-reverts will block further canary increases for 30 minutes unless MediaWorks requests a re-open with remediation notes.
4) Pin duration: if pinned by the revert, the version will remain pinned for up to 24 hours unless extended by mutual written approval.
5) Observability: Redwood will create a dedicated canary dashboard and required alerts; MediaWorks must send request_id and model_version tags to our tracing endpoint.

I've attached the short-form SLA exception for MediaWorks to sign and return (signed_sla_exception_form.docx). Once we receive their signed copy we'll issue the temporary exception and enable the routing/pin behavior in the Canary controller. DocuSign link to follow.

Next steps:
- MediaWorks: review & sign the attached short form + confirm telemetry feed.
- Redwood: schedule a 30-minute onboarding call next Tuesday to wire up tracing and dashboard access.

If that works I’ll route the exception to Sales + Legal for final logging against MW-2026-0943.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: signed_sla_exception_form.docx
